candidates.title: The fix
candidates.concept: Someone rinses one mug in a night kitchen and, without meaning to, reaches for the same chair, the same window, the same thought. The film shows a habit as a groove worn in a day, not a decision, and ends with the smallest possible change: the mug goes on the other side of the sink.
candidates.hook: You did not decide to stand here. Your hands did.
candidates.why: It names something the viewer has done tonight and cannot argue with.

candidates.title: The chair
candidates.concept: A day told only through one kitchen chair: pulled out, sat on, pushed back in, at the same angle every time, until the last shot shows it pulled out somewhere new.
candidates.hook: A chair leg scrapes the same groove in the floor.
candidates.why: A purer visual metaphor for habit, but more abstract and further from the everyday-bias pillar's plain examples.

brief.concept: Someone rinses one mug in a night kitchen and, without meaning to, reaches for the same chair, the same window, the same thought. The film shows a habit as a groove worn in a day, not a decision, and ends with the smallest possible change: the mug goes on the other side of the sink.

hook.line: You did not decide to stand here. Your hands did.
hook.type: a recognition, second person, present tense
hook.why: It names something the viewer has done tonight and cannot argue with.

emotional_arc.purpose: the kitchen ritual, seen as automatic
cue, routine, reward, named in plain words
moving the mug is enough to feel the groove

brief.audience_insight: They know the word habit; what they want is to feel the mechanism in their own kitchen so it stops being an accusation.
brief.narrative_device: a single evening ritual observed twice, the second time with one thing moved
brief.key_message: A habit is a cue you no longer notice. Move the cue and you can feel it.
research_questions: What is the plainest accurate description of the cue-routine-reward loop?
What everyday cues do people report as strongest at night?

motion_promise.reason: The hands moving without thought is the point; two moments of real motion carry it, the rest can hold.

visual_world.setting: a small apartment kitchen at night, one warm pendant lamp, cool blue window
visual_world.lighting: one warm practical against cool ambient, low-key
visual_world.palette_note: deep blue shadows, one amber pool of lamplight, a white mug
visual_world.texture_note: wet ceramic, wooden counter grain, knit sweater, condensation on the window

entities_needed.role: the person whose hands know the kitchen

brief.why_it_works: It turns a concept into a felt moment in a real room, and gives one thing to do that costs nothing.
